1. **The System section is the `v-else` CATCH-ALL.** `app.js:1439` is `<section v-else class="pane">`, **not** `v-else-if="area==='system'"`. `nav-check.mjs:82-84` records this: *"The catch-all. It renders System, so it resolves 'system' and NOTHING else."* **Any new `v-else-if` you add AFTER line 1439 will never render.** Add your markup INSIDE the System section, before its closing `</section>`.
2. **Every new binding must be exported from `setup()`'s return block** (`app.js:548-561`). The vendored Vue browser build compiles templates to `with(_ctx)`, and `render-vm-check.mjs` catches missing identifiers with a Proxy `has` trap. Forget one and the gate goes red — which is the gate working.
3. **There is NO build step and NO charting library.** Vue is vendored (`README.md:9`); `package.json` declares **zero** dependencies. **Do not add one.** The house's only existing "data visual" is a percentage printed as text (`app.js:1445`).
4. **`styles.css:96-106` states the rule verbatim: "LAYOUT ONLY. Not one new colour token."** Every pairing is measured against GL-003 §2b and `contrast-check.mjs` is in-repo and executable.
5. **The doctrine you must not violate, from `app.js:229-237`:** *"'unknown' is GREY, not amber. Amber means 'something is wrong'… Colouring uncertainty as a fault is inventing a fact, just quieter."* This is the whole spirit of AC4.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — the section exists and is reachable.** A **Session / Rotation Reports** group inside the System tab, following the existing `.grp` + `.g-count` heading pattern with a count, rendering **most recent first**. Nav is not regressed: the six existing areas still resolve, and the catch-all still renders System.

**AC2 — the collapsed summary carries exactly what Warwick asked for**, each visible without expanding: session date and time · host and host version · branch · **short closing SHA with the full SHA available** · elapsed time · context tokens in and out · number of specialist dispatches · WO first-dispatch successes · WO amendments · WO refusals · product vs documentation line changes · product/admin/evidence/rework/waiting allocation percentages · unresolved or unestablished measurements · report notes · durable deliverable path.

**AC3 — expansion carries the rest.** Using the existing `<details class="tech">` drawer idiom: the full metric set · **specialist-by-specialist dispatch counts** · specialist token usage where established · specialist notes · **the exact Supabase rotation ID** · the exact closing head · the associated durable Git report path. Unknown values stay labelled as unknown here too.

**AC4 — 🔴 UNKNOWN IS NOT ZERO, and this criterion decides the order.** Warwick, verbatim: *"Do not convert missing values into zero. 'Unknown,' 'not established' and zero are materially different."* A `null` must render as a visibly **unknown** treatment — grey, per the doctrine above — **typographically and tonally distinct from a real `0`**. **Prove it by rendering the supplied fixture, whose first row deliberately contains `woFirstDispatchSuccess: 0` (a true zero) beside `elapsedMinutes: null` and `hostVersion: null` (true unknowns), and showing the two do not look alike.** An empty `unestablished` array and a populated one are also different screens.

**AC5 — visual summaries, hand-rolled, no new tokens.** Concise visuals for: **total context consumption · allocation of effort · WO success/refusal/rework · specialist usage · unresolved measurements.** Build them from the existing primitives — `.tile` numerics, `.chip` state pills (`.ok/.warn/.block/.neutral/.prog`), `.as-kv` `<dl>` fact grids, `.item` tone rails — and, where a bar genuinely helps, hand-rolled CSS using only existing tokens (`--ok-w`, `--accent-w`, `--warn-w`, `--hair`, `--panel2`) **with the number always printed alongside**. **Not one new colour token.** If you believe the surface truly needs one, **stop and say so** — Warwick approves those, not this order.

**AC6 — 🔴 NOTHING IS HARD-CODED.** Warwick, verbatim: *"Do not hard-code those figures. They must be rendered from the stored report data."* For the current report he must plainly see ≈**2.22M subagent tokens** · **15 specialist dispatches** · **26.2%** downstream of preventable defects · **0 of 2** Work Orders surviving first read-back · **three consecutive Keel orders refused on the same contract-surface class** · **88.3%** of insertions documentation · **five proxy-versus-destination verification failures**. **Every one must be derived from the fixture's fields.** The last two live in `gitStat.doc_share_of_insertions_pct` and the `findings` array respectively — render them from there. **A literal `2.22M` or `88.3` anywhere in your diff is an automatic FAIL of this criterion.**

**AC7 — the four states are truthful and distinct.** Loading · empty · load-failure · loaded. Copy the house voice exactly — the AsdAIr packet section at `app.js:691-704` is the model, including that *"not produced"* and *"produced but empty"* are different screens. **A failure to load reports must not break the rest of the System tab** (Warwick's explicit requirement): the failure is contained to this group, with a retry, and *"Happening now"* and *"Recent history"* keep rendering.

**AC8 — the existing gates stay green.** `node services/cockpit/template-check.mjs --self-test && node services/cockpit/template-check.mjs` and `node services/cockpit/render-vm-check.mjs --self-test && node services/cockpit/render-vm-check.mjs` both exit 0, and `node services/cockpit/contrast-check.mjs` exits 0. **Run `--self-test` FIRST every time** — these gates are mutation-tested and a gate that has not been proven to fail is not evidence.

## 📐 THE FROZEN API CONTRACT — Keel is building this in parallel. Build against it; do not vary it.

`GET /api/rotation-reports` → HTTP 200. Failure is **also** HTTP 200 with `{ "ok": false, "error": "<human sentence>" }` — that is the house pattern, so **do not branch on HTTP status; branch on `ok`.**

```jsonc
{
  "ok": true,
  "reports": [                       // most recent first; [] when empty
    {
      "id": "2274c7ae-…",            // exact Supabase rotation id — render verbatim (AC3)
      "createdAt": "2026-08-07T00:38:45.516Z",
      "sessionDate": "2026-08-07",
      "host": "claude",
      "hostVersion": null,           // null is COMMON — the AC4 adversarial case
      "branch": "build-020/phase4-automation-law",
      "closingHead": "ccb4132e6d13a8f2e34f80019b8fefa79cdb1a6f",
      "closingHeadShort": "ccb4132",
      "mapPath": "Deliverables/…",
      "deliverablePath": "Deliverables/…",   // the durable Git report path (AC2, AC3)
      "elapsedMinutes": null,
      "contextTokensIn": null,
      "contextTokensOut": null,
      "subagentTokens": 2221596,     // → "≈2.22M" (AC6) — FORMAT it, never write it
      "specialistDispatches": 15,
      "workOrders": { "total": 2, "firstDispatchSuccess": 0, "amendments": 0, "refusals": 2 },
      "lines": { "docChanged": 1667, "productChanged": 313 },
      "gitStat": { "insertions": 1834, "deletions": 146,
                   "doc_share_of_insertions_pct": 88.3, … },   // → the 88.3% (AC6)
      "allocation": { "productPct": 21.7, "adminPct": 8.9, "evidencePct": 29.9,
                      "reworkPct": 26.2, "waitingPct": null },  // reworkPct → the 26.2% (AC6)
      "findings": [ { "id": "F1", "text": "Three consecutive Keel Work Orders…",
                      "confidence": "high" }, … ],              // → both remaining AC6 figures
      "unestablished": [ "opening_context_tokens", … ],
      "notes": "…",
      "specialists": [ { "specialist": "veritas", "dispatches": 4,
                         "tokensIn": null, "tokensOut": null, "notes": "…" } ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Any field may be `null`. `specialists` and `findings` may be `[]`. Neither is an error.** If you think the contract is wrong, **return and say so — do not silently improve it**, because Keel is building the other side of it and cannot see your change.
